import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: 'data/customer_segments.csv' not found.")
    print("Please make sure the dataset is in the 'data' directory.")
    # As a fallback for environments without the file, create a dummy dataframe
    data = {
        'Income': [58138.0, 46344.0, 71613.0, 26646.0, 58293.0, 85000.0, 95000.0, 35000.0, 150000.0],
        'Kidhome': [0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0],
        'Teenhome': [0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0],
        'MntWines': [635, 11, 426, 11, 173, 520, 800, 50, 1000],
        'MntFruits': [88, 1, 49, 4, 43, 40, 30, 5, 100],
        'MntMeatProducts': [546, 6, 127, 20, 118, 150, 250, 30, 800],
        'MntFishProducts': [172, 2, 111, 10, 46, 50, 60, 3, 200],
        'MntSweetProducts': [88, 1, 21, 3, 27, 40, 10, 2, 150],
        'MntGoldProds': [88, 6, 42, 5, 15, 30, 20, 1, 100]
    }
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# --- Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering ---

# Drop rows with missing income values for accurate plotting
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Create a 'Total_Spending' column by summing all spending categories
mnt_cols = [col for col in df.columns if 'Mnt' in col]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Create a 'Children_Count' column for easier segmentation
df['Children_Count'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']

# Filter out extreme income outliers for a clearer visualization of the main data cluster
df_filtered = df[(df['Income'] < 200000) & (df['Income'] > 0)].copy()

# Convert Children_Count to a categorical type for better handling by seaborn's hue
df_filtered['Children_Count'] = df_filtered['Children_Count'].astype('category')


# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatter plot
# This plot explores the relationship between income and spending, segmented by the number of children.
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Children_Count',
    palette='viridis_r',
    alpha=0.7,
    s=60,
    edgecolor='w',
    linewidth=0.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labeling for Clarity ---

# Set a clear and descriptive title
ax.set_title('Customer Spending Habits: Income vs. Total Spending by Household Size',
             fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)

# Set informative axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Household Income', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Spending on Products (Last 2 Years)', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)

# Format axis ticks to be more readable (e.g., $50,000)
formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x:,.0f}')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')

# Customize the legend
legend = ax.get_legend()
legend.set_title('Number of Children')
legend.get_title().set_fontsize('12')
for text in legend.get_texts():
    text.set_fontsize('10')

# Add a regression line to show the overall trend
sns.regplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    scatter=False,
    color='#e74c3c',
    line_kws={'linestyle':'--', 'linewidth':2},
    ax=ax,
    label='Overall Trend' # Add label for the legend
)

# Manually add the regression line to the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# The regplot adds its own handle/label, so we need to re-create the legend
# to include it and style it properly.
# We slice to combine the scatter handles with our new trend line handle.
ax.legend(handles=handles, labels=labels, title='Number of Children',
          title_fontsize='12', fontsize='10', loc='upper left')

# Add a text annotation to highlight the main takeaway
ax.text(0.95, 0.05, 'Higher income generally correlates with higher spending,\n'
                    'but households with no children tend to spend more\n'
                    'at similar income levels.',
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=10,
        verticalalignment='bottom', horizontalalignment='right',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.5', fc='aliceblue', alpha=0.8))

# Adjust layout and save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
